assets.label: NASA Blue Marble cloud layer · Blue Marble 2002 cloud composite (constituent days unstated)
assets.credit: NASA Goddard / Reto Stockli (clouds) and Robert Simmon (compositing)
assets.limitations: Historical visual reference published in 2002. NASA describes the clouds as two days of visible imagery and a third day of thermal-infrared imagery over the poles; exact dates and instruments are unstated, and an earlier review recorded manually filled regions. The layer contains no surface: land, ocean and land ice come from the separately dated July 2004 land map, so clouds and surface are not simultaneous observations. Opacity reproduces NASA's 2002 composite within the documented residual; it is not a physical cloud transmission. No current weather, cloud height, optical depth or feature-position measurement may be inferred. The source JPEG has no geotags or ICC profile; registration is reviewed for display, not measurement. Night lights remain a separately dated annual reference.
assets.derivation: tools/prepare_earth_clouds.py with Pillow 12.2.0: the NASA JPEG decodes to identical R, G and B in every pixel; each output pixel is white RGB with alpha from the tool's pinned 256-entry opacity curve applied to that source byte, encoded as a deterministic RGBA PNG without resampling, filling or colour change. Opacity curve: over dark-ocean 24-pixel blocks with a cloud-free base in NASA's 2002 land/ocean/ice/cloud composite (record 57735), the linear-light opacity each grey value implies is taken as a median, interpolated and made monotone; --fit-opacity reproduces it from both pinned originals. On 490 held-out blocks the curve fitted on the other blocks gives mean encoded error 11.48/255 over ocean, 13.69/255 over land and 17.35/255 in thin haze, against 14.64, 17.76 and 22.81 for alpha equal to grey. Display registration (reviewed): after a 9-pixel high-pass, source brightness between about 70 degrees north and south correlates with the darkest channel of the coastline-registered composite at r=0.823 at zero offset, 0.572 one pixel east or west, 0.485 one pixel north or south and 0.031 half a map away, so it shares that composite's north-up, eastward, Greenwich u=0.5, full-latitude grid. This is display-registration and display-opacity evidence, not a geotag or a scientific cloud retrieval. The source PNG is unchanged. Cloud depth mode applies an artistic display remap: 0.9 * max(0, (alpha - 0.08) / 0.92)^1.5 before converting to optical density. This reduces thin haze; it is not a retrieved optical depth.

assets.limitations: Cloud-free nights selected over each land mass A display composite, not instantaneous city lights or an outage measurement No radiometric interpretation of display intensities.

assets.label: NASA Blue Marble land and ice · July 2004
assets.limitations: Historical July 2004 monthly composite, chosen for the default surface view; not a simulation of the current season. Deep ocean uses assigned uniform blue. Temporal and spatial gaps are filled by the provider. Arctic ocean is blue in this original; no synthetic polar cap is added.
